purpose: A privacy-first conversational wizard that analyzes pasted disk-usage reports and produces risk-ranked cleanup plans with exact commands, primarily for Windows.
does: Six-step workflow: gather context (OS, drive, free space, goal) → recommend WinDirStat/WizTree (`winget install WinDirStat.WinDirStat`) → hand over `scripts/disk_analyzer.py` → parse the pasted report → generate tailored PowerShell → close the loop with Storage Sense habits
Ranks every suggestion by (reclaimable GB × safety), leading with Recycle Bin, temp, old Downloads and Windows Update cache; flags AppData/Program Files/hibernation with alternatives
Buckets findings into Quick Wins / Review & Decide / Investigate Further, always offering 'move to Archive' before permanent delete and `-WhatIf` before execution
Handles special cases: describing a treemap visually, duplicates, macOS (DaisyDisk/GrandPerspective) and Linux (`ncdu`/`baobab`), dev machines (node_modules, target/, .cache, Docker/WSL volumes)
output_type: prioritized cleanup plan + generated PowerShell scripts
trigger_summary: "Triggers on low disk space, cleaning drive, finding large files or folders, WinDirStat, C drive full, storage management, or freeing up space."
provenance_signals: **Ported from Grok, and the port is incomplete.** `scripts/disk_analyzer.py` docstring: "Then copy the entire Markdown output and paste it back to **Grok** (disk-cleanup-wizard skill will activate automatically...)" — the original host is named in shipped code. Also third-person persona framing ("You are a careful, expert storage management assistant"), a style marker of ported system prompts. No author, no license, no version.
knowledge_type: mixed — ~55% durable_external_knowledge (Windows space-hog taxonomy in `references/windows-space-hogs-and-safe-cleanup.md`, the exact winget package id, Storage Sense, hiberfil/pagefile semantics, per-OS tool names) / ~30% workflow_procedure (the six-step loop and three-bucket output) / ~15% generic_reasoning (safety framing)
external_deps: `scripts/disk_analyzer.py` — EXISTS ✓, stdlib-only Python 3.6+, runs on the USER'S machine not here
`references/windows-space-hogs-and-safe-cleanup.md` — EXISTS ✓
WinDirStat / WizTree via winget, choco or scoop — user-side, Windows-only
PowerShell on the user's machine
By design requires NO access to this filesystem — the whole skill runs on pasted text
overlap_with: vps-devops rule — that rule owns disk pressure on VPS 94.72.104.81 (df -h thresholds, the ordered `docker image prune` / `journalctl --vacuum-size` cleanup sequence). This skill would give generic Windows advice for a problem the repo has a precise Linux runbook for.
async-runner — adjacent 'watch machine resources' framing
risk_notes: Wrong platform for this environment: CircleTel's real disk problem is a Linux VPS running Coolify, and `.claude/rules/vps-devops.md` already prescribes a safe-cleanup order that explicitly forbids dropping Coolify app/db/redis containers. This skill knows none of that and its Linux branch is a one-line `ncdu`/`baobab` aside. If it triggers on "disk full" during VPS work it will actively displace the correct runbook. The Grok reference left in shipped code is a provenance leak that would confuse a user who runs the script and reads its instructions. Safety design itself is sound — no direct file access, `-WhatIf` first, archive-before-delete.
